command: python -m fdtd.modes sensitivity --output reports/tolerance/geometry-sensitivity.json  # single alignment; then python scripts/rerun_sensitivity_averaged.py once with axis=z and once with axis=x; then python scripts/merge_sensitivity_per_axis.py
notes: P5 input, not a P5 result: no gate is evaluated here.
The scenario design document is referenced, not hashed: it evolves as further axes are measured, and hashing it here would invalidate every measurement record on each edit.
SiN is ~9.8x less width-sensitive than Si. G1 removed the numerical case for switching platform; this is a physical one.
Supersedes P5-0002, which used single-alignment derivatives. Per-axis offset averaging corrected the width derivative by 9-10% and the height derivative by 23-27%.
Each axis average moves only its own derivative and leaves the other inside 1%; the full xz outer product (160 solves) was therefore skipped.
The epsilon relaxation widens the linewidth 4.6x and therefore relaxes the tolerance requirement by the same factor.
Even so, 1 nm of width error is ~23 linewidths on SiN at the working Q: active trim is part of the architecture.
Thermal trim shares a channel with the thermal dynamics the design intends to use; P2 must separate them.

title: Geometry to resonance sensitivity (P5 scenario-design input)
uncertainty_method: central difference at +-1 nm, per-axis sub-cell offset averaged over four placements; the quoted systematic is the alignment swing, not the mesh-to-mesh difference
validity: Straight waveguide cross-section at 1550 nm, single TE core mode, no bend, no coupler, no supermode. Sensitivities are local derivatives, valid for small excursions only.
